result.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx the onError handler constructs `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Template literals are never falsy, so the fallback is dead code, and when err.data is undefined users see an 'undefined: <err.message>' prefix (with t() applied to a raw server error string like 'booking_not_found'). This mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. Because this is a template literal, `message` will always be a non-empty string (e.g., if `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `'undefined: ...'`, and even if `t(err.message)` returns an empty string it still yields at least `'undefined: '`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback translation, and users may see an `undefined:` prefix when `err.data?.code` is missing.
